text_en: A senior policy official at Colombia's central bank said the country may need to raise interest rates further and keep them high for longer to curb rising inflation risks. Co-director of Colombia's central bank Mauricio Villamizar said El Niño, the Iran war and a large fiscal deficit could all intensify price pressures. "We expect rates to remain high for longer, but further hikes are also on the table if necessary," Villamizar said Tuesday in an interview during the IMF annual meetings in Bangkok. Colombia unexpectedly raised rates last month, lifting them to the highest level since 2024.
